Spain's peaceful transition to democracy after 1975, culminating in the democratic Constitution approved in 1978.
Spain's system of government: the monarch is head of state while elected representatives in the Cortes make the laws.
Grassroots protest movements such as the 'indignados' of 15-M, who occupied Spanish squares in May 2011 against austerity and corruption.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Aspects of Political Life in the Hispanic World — a core area of A-Level Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Aspects of Political Life in the Hispanic World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Aspects of Political Life in the Hispanic World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Franco's dictatorship in Spain ended in which way?
options: With his death in 1975
With a military defeat by France
With elections held in 1950
It continues today

mcqs.q: The Spanish 'indignados' movement (15-M) began in which year?
What system of government does Spain have today?
options: A parliamentary monarchy
An absolute monarchy
A military junta
A one-party state

mcqs.q: Augusto Pinochet led a dictatorship in which Spanish-speaking country?
options: Chile
Mexico
Cuba
Uruguay

mcqs.q: When did 'la transición' to democracy take place in Spain?
options: Spain has had no head of state since 1978.
The transición took place during the First World War.
After Franco's death in 1975, leading to the democratic Constitution of 1978.
The transición happened straight after the Civil War ended in 1939.

mcqs.q: Does the Spanish king govern the country?
options: El rey makes Spain's laws and runs the government.
The transición took place during the First World War.
No - in a parliamentary monarchy the king reigns as head of state, while the elected government and the Cortes govern.
Spain has had no head of state since 1978.
No - it was a grassroots protest movement of 2011; the party Podemos was founded later, in 2014, partly inspired by it.
Los indignados was the name of a party that stood in elections.
Spain has had no head of state since 1978.
Los indignados was a Spanish football supporters' club.
